cards.text: Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus, is writing to the saints in Ephesus. He just prayed they'd know the surpassing greatness of God's power, the same power God used to raise Christ from the dead and seat Him at His right hand. Now Paul turns to his readers and reminds them where they were before all that.

cards.question: How does Paul describe his readers back then, in their trespasses and sins?

cards.text: Not tired. Not hitting snooze. DEAD! And Paul says they used to walk in those sins, following the ways of this world and of the ruler of the power of the air.

cards.question: Paul calls the ruler of the power of the air a spirit. True or false: Paul says that spirit has stopped working.

cards.text: Then Paul describes a life of fulfilling the cravings of the flesh and indulging its desires and thoughts.

cards.question: Who does Paul say lived that way at one time?

answers.text: All of us with Paul included

cards.text: Paul could have stuck with you. Instead he says all of us. That's a man who remembers where he came from, and so do I, friend: a 25 cent bin.

cards.question: True or false: Paul says that by nature, he and his readers were children of wrath, like the rest.

cards.text: Dead. Wrong ruler. Children of wrath. If this were a weather report, I'd stay in bed. Then Paul flips everything with one little word: But.

cards.question: Why does God step in for people who were dead in their sins?

answers.text: Because of His great love for us
Because they had earned a second chance
Because they finally cried out to Him

cards.text: Paul says God is rich in mercy. Not a pinch of it saved for emergencies, friend. RICH! And God made us alive with Christ.

cards.question: True or false: God made them alive with Christ only after they stopped living in their trespasses.

cards.text: Then, right in the middle of his thought, Paul can't hold it in. I bet he wanted to jump out of his chair, the way I hop on my gold base when a batch comes out PERFECT.

cards.question: Paul exclaims: "It is by ___ you have been saved!"

cards.text: Remember Paul's prayer: God raised Christ from the dead and seated Him at His right hand in the heavenly realms. Now Paul tells us what God did for us, together with Christ.

cards.question: What does Paul say God did for us, with Christ?

answers.text: Raised us up and seated us with Him
Sent us out to stand guard for Him
Told us to wait at the gate for Him

cards.text: Seated, friend. Not hovering by the door hoping somebody saves you a spot. SEATED, in the heavenly realms in Christ Jesus!

cards.question: Why did God do all this, according to Paul?

answers.text: To display the riches of His grace
To display the strength of His people
To display His anger at the world

cards.text: Then Paul comes back to that grace line from before. This time he adds how it happens.

cards.question: "For it is by grace you have been saved through ___"
Paul says this salvation is not from yourselves. So what is it?

cards.text: A gift, friend. I didn't stamp my way out of that junk drawer; I was lying in the back under the paper and the dust when the light came in. And Paul says it's not by works.

cards.question: Why does Paul say salvation is not by works?

answers.text: So that no one can boast
So that no one gets worn out
So that no one gets left behind

cards.text: So nobody gets to post "Saved myself, no big deal" in the group chat. Then Paul says we are God's workmanship, created in Christ Jesus.

cards.question: Paul says we're God's workmanship, created in Christ Jesus. Created to do what?

answers.text: To judge the works of others

cards.text: Not saved BY good works, friend. Created FOR them. One is a ticket you could never afford, and the other is the work you were made to do.

cards.question: True or false: Paul says it's up to us to plan those good works ourselves.

cards.text: God prepared them in advance as our way of life. That's like walking into the bakery and finding the oven already warm. Somebody was expecting you!
